title: 1988 AHSME Problem 26
statement: Suppose that \(p\) and \(q\) are positive numbers for which \[ \begin{aligned} \log_9(p)&=\log_{12}(q)\\ &=\log_{16}(p+q). \end{aligned} \] What is the value of \(\frac{q}{p}?\)

solutions.text:
Let the common value be \(t.\) Then \(p=9^t,\ q=12^t,\) and \(p+q=16^t.\) Put \(r=\frac{q}{p}=(\frac{4}{3})^t.\) Dividing the last equation by \(p\) gives \[ \begin{aligned} 1+r&=(\frac{16}{9})^t\\ &=((\frac{4}{3})^t)^2=r^2. \end{aligned} \] Since \(r>0,\) \(r=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}.\)

Thus the correct answer is D.
